transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... well, I came in because I just keep getting these, um, these nagging thoughts that I forgot something really important. Like, I'll worry that I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong. She takes these tiny little pink pills for her blood pressure, and her doctor just switched her dosage last month because the old one was making her dizzy. Which is terrifying because she has all these steep hardwood stairs in her house, and I keep telling her she needs to look into a single-story place, maybe over by the new shopping center where it's a bit flatter... but anyway, yeah, I just get stuck on the medicine thing. 

Or I'll worry about not setting up my classroom materials safely. I teach fourth grade, and the kids just get into absolutely everything. Just last week, Tommy—he's a sweet boy, but his mom just had a baby so he's acting out a lot for attention—he almost knocked over this entire science display I spent three hours building on a Sunday. I had to go to three different craft stores just to find the right kind of foam board for it. 

But yeah, it's just... even when I know I probably handled things fine and made sure everything was put away right, the doubt just keeps popping back into my head.

Do you find yourself worrying about other things outside of these specific situations, like your health, job performance, or other responsibilities, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to be concerned?

Um, no, not really. Like, I don't really stress about my health or my job performance overall. Actually, my principal just gave me a really glowing evaluation a few weeks ago. He's usually pretty strict, too, but lately he's been super distracted because they're finally repaving the staff parking lot, which has been just a total nightmare. I had to park three blocks away on Tuesday, right in front of this little bakery that sells these amazing lemon scones. I usually try to avoid too much sugar during the week, but I just couldn't resist. My sister always tells me sugar is why I get so tired in the afternoons, but she reads all those crazy wellness blogs, you know? She just bought this three-hundred-dollar cold-press juicer that takes up her entire kitchen counter, and she's trying to convince me to do a celery cleanse. But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, other worries. No, I don't really sit around worrying about general things like that. It's really just the specific stuff I mentioned, like the medicine and making sure the classroom is safe.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over, like checking, counting, or repeating actions in your mind to feel more certain or to reduce the worry?

Yeah, I guess I do. Like, before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll go back over the same things a few times. I'll check my aunt's pill organizer, or my stove... oh, my stove is this vintage gas one from the 1950s, I think? It’s this gorgeous mint green color, which is honestly the whole reason I signed the lease, but the knobs are incredibly loose. You just brush past them and they turn! My neighbor told me her cat actually turned hers on once, which is terrifying. I don't have a cat, I'm way more of a dog person, but my building has a strict fifteen-pound weight limit, so a Golden Retriever is completely out of the question, which just breaks my heart. 

But anyway, yeah, I'll check the stove, or my lesson plans at school. Sometimes I just stand there silently replaying what I did in my head, just to be absolutely sure I didn't leave anything dangerous out. I just have to keep doing it until I feel calm enough to actually move on. 

It does make me run late sometimes, though. Just Tuesday I was running late because of it and I missed the good traffic light cycle on Oak Street. If you don't hit that green light by exactly 7:15, you get stuck behind all the middle school buses, and they stop at literally every single block. The drivers are so patient though... my uncle was a bus driver for thirty years before he retired to Florida. He lives right near Orlando now, so we always try to visit him around the holidays, though the airfare is getting ridiculous. 

Wait, sorry, what was I... oh, right. Yes, I do go back and check things or replay them in my head before I can leave.
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors upset you a lot or interfere with your day-to-day life, like making you late for work or causing arguments with people close to you?

Um, I mean, I’m still getting through everything mostly fine. Like, I still handle my work and family commitments. But my mornings definitely take a lot longer now because of all the checking. I end up arriving at school feeling so rushed and behind before the day even starts. Which is honestly the worst feeling, especially when you have to fight for the good copy machine in the staff room. Mr. Henderson, the fifth-grade teacher, always uses the wrong paper weight and jams it. He insists on printing these massive thirty-page packets for his history unit. I keep telling him he should just put them on the Google Classroom, but he’s one of those teachers who just absolutely refuses to learn new technology. He actually still uses an overhead projector sometimes! Remember those? With the wet-erase markers that always got all over the side of your hand? I used to love the smell of them when I was a kid, but it's just so outdated now. 

But anyway, yeah, I get to school feeling behind. And then at night, my lesson prep and my evening journaling just... they don’t feel as smooth or restorative as they used to. I love journaling, I’ve been doing it since I was in middle school. I use these specific dotted notebooks, the A5 size, and I have to use this one brand of Japanese gel pen because otherwise the ink bleeds right through the page. I actually order the pens in bulk online, but my last package got lost in the mail for three weeks. The tracking said it was sitting in Seattle, and I live nowhere near Seattle, so I had to call the post office and the lady on the phone was just so unhelpful... 

Wait, sorry, what were you asking? Oh, if it upsets me. Yeah, I guess it’s just frustrating that things like my journaling and lesson prep aren’t relaxing anymore, and my mornings are just a lot more stressful than they need to be. But I'm still getting everything done, you know?
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to function in areas of your life like work, socializing, or spending time with loved ones?

Um, didn't I kind of just answer that? Or wait, do you mean specifically with like, my friends and family? Because no, I wouldn't say it stops me from socializing or anything. I'm still seeing people. Like, we actually just went out for my friend Sarah's birthday on Friday. We went to this new tapas place downtown, which was supposed to be a total surprise, but her husband completely ruined it because he left the reservation confirmation up on their shared iPad. I don't know why they still share an iPad, honestly, they both have their own phones. 

But anyway, the restaurant was incredibly loud, and they charged like fourteen dollars for literally three tiny dates wrapped in bacon. I could make that at home for two dollars! I actually really love cooking, especially now that it's fall. I make this incredible roasted butternut squash soup, and I usually bring leftovers to the teachers' lounge. Everyone loves it, except for the new gym teacher who is on some extremely strict keto diet. He won't even eat carrots because he says they have too many carbs, which just sounds absolutely miserable to me. I can't imagine living without bread, let alone carrots. 

But um... sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? What did you ask? Oh, right, distress and functioning. Yeah, no, it doesn't really stop me from doing things or seeing my loved ones. Like I was saying before, I'm still getting by totally fine, it's really just that it makes my mornings annoying. So no, I wouldn't say it's ruining my social life or anything like that.
How much time do these checking behaviors and thoughts take up in your day — like, would you say it's more than an hour total, or less than that?

Um, I haven't really timed it or anything. It doesn't feel like it takes up a huge chunk of my day. Maybe less than an hour? It's hard to say. I mean, time is so weird anyway, especially in the mornings. You know how you can look at the clock and it's 6:30, and then you blink and suddenly it's 7:10 and you haven't even brushed your teeth yet? I actually just bought this new alarm clock that's supposed to mimic the sunrise to help with that. It slowly lights up your room over thirty minutes before the alarm actually goes off. It was pretty expensive, I had to order it from this specialty sleep website, but I figured it was worth it because the winters here get so dark. 

I hate waking up when it's pitch black outside. It makes me feel like I'm waking up in the middle of the night. My sister lives in Alaska, right up near Fairbanks, and she says they only get like three hours of daylight in the dead of winter. I have no idea how she does it. She has one of those full-spectrum light boxes she sits in front of while she drinks her coffee. She actually roasts her own coffee beans, which is such a hipster thing to do, but it does smell amazing when she sends me a bag. She sent me this Ethiopian blend for my birthday...

Wait, sorry. Time. You were asking about time. Yeah, I don't think it's more than an hour total. Just those little bits in the morning mostly.

This supports ruling out F43.2 (adjustment disorder with anxiety) and maintaining F42.9 (obsessive-compulsive disorder, unspecified) as the most likely diagnosis.
